perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s available perspective:

- I am a construction worker; Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist at my construction company. We have a friendly but professional relationship, mostly when I visit the office for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, I noticed Elizabeth was unusually curt/short with me over several days. I wondered if I had upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknowing mistake.
- I asked her if I had done something to upset her. She told me no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.
- I felt sympathetic and offered to listen, suggesting a coffee break. She accepted, said it was kind, and thanked me.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses. They seemed severe to me. I suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can help. She said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant.
- Afterward, I noticed she became slightly withdrawn. I worried I may have overstepped or embarrassed her, so I told her I hoped I hadn’t overstepped and that I support her. She said I hadn’t overstepped, appreciated my concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative. I believed she valued my support and felt more comfortable around me. I told her I was glad we talked and that I’m always available to chat or take a break. She thanked me, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had my support.
- I intend to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.
